summary_paragraph: A 54-year-old woman with a complex medical history including Crohn’s disease, SVC syndrome, and PTSD was admitted for high fevers, nausea, vomiting, and recurrent right thigh pain following a recent hospitalization for a groin hematoma and SVC recanalization. Initial concern was recurrence of the hematoma, but ultrasound showed complete resolution. A CT scan revealed no Crohn’s flare or bowel obstruction but identified a small 3 cm fluid collection in the right thigh, likely a minor hematoma. The patient was managed with an NG tube for gastric dysmotility and IV medications for pain, nausea, and anxiety. She remained afebrile after admission, and extensive workup found no infectious source. Symptoms improved with supportive care, and she was discharged on a taper of Dilaudid and diphenhydramine, with instructions for port care, medication management, and follow-up.
